reachable: Yes, and verified by execution rather than by reading. to_obs left-multiplies the prediction by a single 768x768 buffer with no branch on z_prev, on any observation, on the window or on the arm, so it is bit-identically the same map at the scored position under the native and the role-swapped chain, and it is unaffected by the read's observation being withheld. The map is genuinely non-identity by scoring time: buffers are updated once per training step from make_target, the first rebuild fires at step 300 of the 4000-step budget (eval/adapter.py defaults to 4000; the genome sets no optim steps), and roughly 25 rebuilds occur. Replaying the real batcher over the real standardized targets, fwd_map deviates from I by max |.| 1.22 at step 300 and 1.45 by step 600, while at step 299 it is exactly I. The inverse is exact as claimed: max |F^-1 F - I| = 1.5e-7 in float64 and 2.5e-6 through the float32 buffers. eval/adapter.py deep-copies net.target_module before probing, so the trained maps do reach the probe. The target module has no trainable parameters (buffers only, EMA-updated under no_grad), which matches the precedent set by zca_shrunk_target_whitening; it therefore gets no gradient itself, but it reshapes the loss the whole net sees for ~92% of training. Note that eval/guard_reach.py runs a single step, so at gate time the map is exactly the identity — the reachability gate certifies the arch/head, not this mechanism. Cost measured on CPU only: 7.3 ms per step for the moment update plus neighbour search on 1916 rows, 93 ms per rebuild; both small against a real forward/backward.
solves_outside_model: No. Nothing resolves the move chain outside the net and feeds the answer in. The target module never sees a command — make_target and to_obs take only z_obs / pred, and the confusion moment is estimated purely from the marginal geometry of the observation-target distribution. The batcher parses commands (mv / cp / redirect) to label routed-read depth, but only to CHOOSE which sequence indices go into a batch; it returns a list[int] and never touches model input. The head reads command and observation embeddings that are already the model's own input tokens, and only to mine training triples and shape an aux loss; its stash path and mining are guarded by torch.is_grad_enabled() and mod.training. The forward-time copy-transport contribution is the parent's mechanism, unchanged. The only thing that acts on the model's input/output at scoring time is one fixed global linear map applied to the prediction, arm-invariant and window-invariant, which cannot carry role-dependent information into comp_ca.
summary:
The code is coherent, self-contained and does implement the artifact it describes: two EMA second-moment buffers, a shrunk whitener, a whitened-discriminant gain, an algebraically exact inverse, live at the scored position and identical across arms. The chunk DESCRIPTION strings are accurate about mechanism, and nothing leaks. What does not survive measurement is the hypothesis's causal story, on four of its five load-bearing claims.

(1) The stated premise is false in the space the model trains in. The harness standardizes targets per dimension, so there is no dominant shared component to compress — the global mean carries 0.12% of target energy, two exposed contents in one window are only cosine 0.19 apart (vs 0.035 for random pairs), and their squared distance is already 0.90x that of two random contentful observations. The claim that "the routing-dependent part of the target is a small fraction of the loss" is further undercut because the inherited objective's dominant term is a listwise NCE, not squared error.

(2) The effect on the eval's actual confusables runs the other way. Within a foil pair the map does tilt energy from the shared half toward the differing half (0.677 -> 1.012), but that is 1.49x, not "the majority of the loss". Across pairs — which is what the contrastive objective weighs — the transformed distance between two same-window exposed contents relative to a random contentful pair FALLS 3x (0.899 -> 0.301). The map de-emphasizes precisely the subspace §2 says it expands.

(3) The invention itself is inert. Ablating the confusion moment entirely and keeping only the shrunk ZCA whitener moves those two numbers by 0.1% and 2%. The gain spectrum never reaches its clamp (g in [0.34, 1.82]) while the whitener spans a 57x singular-value spread. Whatever this candidate does to the target metric is shrunk ZCA whitening, which is already in the chunk pool three times.

(4) §4's "this is not a free extra" is falsified twice. In-batch nearest-neighbour pairs are same-sequence 1.0% of the time with this batcher vs 0.9% uniform — chance, because _accumulate_confusion strides the batch to ~3 rows per sequence — and the map built with baseline_uniform is numerically indistinguishable (0.2981 vs 0.3014).

(5) §3's head disjointness is false in the harmful direction. 24.6% of the change-rule's mined triples lie entirely inside cups, dominated by ('cat','mv','mv') and ('mv','mv','cat') — supervising the shared transition operator that mv rewrites a file's content into, and out of, the constant empty-mv observation. The hypothesis says this rule "structurally rejects every cups triple" and that the crossover teaches the operator that mv carries content unchanged. The preserving rule likewise mines 775 cvar triples of 1490, not zero.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: I never trained the genome, so I have no comp_ca and no statement about whether the candidate beats its parent — and at a 0.0227 noise floor on three seeds, the geometric facts above do not determine the sign of the outcome. I measured the static geometry of the target metric, not the trained net's error distribution, so the interaction with r22's per-dimension precision clamp [0.25, 4] under real optimization is unmeasured (the author flagged this himself). Cost is CPU-only. The head's mis-supervision of mv is a mined-triple count, not a measured degradation of the operator.

divergences.claim: (hypothesis §1b) The candidates that must be told apart 'differ only in a canary token ... a small-norm direction sitting inside a much larger shared component. Under the identity target, squared error and every distance in the loss are dominated by the shared component ... The routing-dependent part of the target is a small fraction of the loss.'
divergences.what_the_code_does: The premise is measurably false on the targets the model is actually trained on. The harness standardizes z_obs per dimension (eval/adapter.py -> M.apply_stats), which removes the shared mean by construction. Measured on the real inner-split cups windows: E||mean target||^2 = 0.906 against E||target||^2 = 770.4 (the global shared component is 0.12% of target energy). Within a foil pair (the two exposed contents of one window) the differing half already carries 68% of the energy of the shared half (mean cosine between two exposed contents = 0.193, vs 0.035 for random pairs), and the squared distance between two same-window contents (1666) is 0.90x the squared distance between two random contentful observations (1853) — i.e. the eval's confusables are already about as far apart as arbitrary pairs, not a small direction buried in a shared component. Separately, the inherited objective's dominant term is a listwise NCE over in-batch targets (weight 1) in which a component common to all candidates largely cancels; the plain squared-error anchor carries weight 0.05.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/rev27/p6.py, p7.py, p8.py against data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd (train frame, inner split, 640 windows / 3148 foil pairs): identity  foilpair^2 1666.07  randpair^2(contentful) 1852.88  ratio 0.899 | mean-target^2 0.906  target^2 770.40  shared-frac 0.0012; cosine(exposed_a, exposed_b) mean 0.193 med 0.190; ||diff/2||^2 / ||mean||^2 = 0.681.

divergences.claim: (hypothesis §2) 'The shared component of the target ... is compressed, and the component that distinguishes one exposed content from another is expanded' / 'Re-metrizing the target makes the content-distinguishing subspace the majority of the loss, so the cheapest remaining way to lower the loss is to identify WHICH exposed content the read returns.'
divergences.what_the_code_does: Directionally present but weak in the narrow sense and reversed in the sense that governs the objective. Within a foil pair, F does tilt energy from the shared half to the differing half: diff/shared goes 0.677 (identity) -> 1.012 (F), a 1.49x tilt — 40% of the pair's energy becomes 50%, not 'the majority of the loss'. Across pairs, which is what the listwise contrast actually weighs, F pushes the eval's hard candidates DOWN: the transformed squared distance between two same-window exposed contents relative to two random contentful observations falls from 0.899 (identity) to 0.301 (F), a 3x de-emphasis of exactly the subspace the hypothesis says is expanded. This is the ordinary consequence of whitening: the foil differences lie along high-variance directions of the target distribution, so S^-1/2 compresses them.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/rev27/p8.py, p11.py: identity diff/shared 0.6772, foil/contentful-rand 0.8992; F full diff/shared 1.0117, foil/contentful-rand 0.3014. F built by replaying the real batcher over the real standardized training targets for 1200 steps (buffers converge in ~100 steps at momentum 0.99).

divergences.claim: (hypothesis §2, the stated invention) The confusion moment G — nearest NON-DUPLICATE neighbour differences, inverse-duplicate-class weighting, the whitened-discriminant gain (mu/mean mu)^(p/2) — is 'the mechanism neither program has' and is what stretches the confusable directions.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The confusion-moment layer is essentially inert. Ablating the gain (setting V diag(g) V^T = I, leaving only the shrunk ZCA whitener B = S_n^-1/2 that the module also builds) changes the two quantities the hypothesis is about by 0.1% and 2%: diff/shared 1.0108 (ZCA only) vs 1.0117 (full F); foil/contentful-rand 0.3072 (ZCA only) vs 0.3014 (full F). The measured gain spectrum is mild and never hits its clamp (g in [0.340, 1.823], 0 of 768 directions clamped), while the whitener it multiplies has eigenvalues of s_norm spanning 0.052 to 167.8 (singular-value spread 57x in B). So whatever this candidate does to the target metric is a shrunk ZCA whitening, which already exists in the chunk pool three times (zca_shrunk_target_whitening, ridge_zca_whitened_obs, r2_shrunk_zca_content_metric).
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/rev27/p1.py (gain min/med/max 0.3404/0.9429/1.8234, 0 at either clamp; lam(s_norm) 0.0523..167.80) and p11.py (ZCA-only vs full-F rows).

divergences.claim: (hypothesis §4) The batcher 'is load-bearing rather than decoration': image-blocking the remainder 'makes the in-batch nearest neighbours the same kind of confusable the scored position faces, so G estimates the right subspace', where uniform sampling would make G measure between-system differences.
divergences.what_the_code_does: No measurable effect on either the neighbour geometry or the resulting map. With the slot27 batcher, 1.0% of the mined nearest-neighbour pairs come from the same sequence and 18.9% from the same image; with baseline_uniform, 0.9% and 13.5%. The 1% same-sequence rate is what pure chance gives, because _accumulate_confusion strides the flattened batch (n≈1875 command rows, subsample 192 -> stride 9), leaving ~3 rows per sequence out of 192 candidates. So G is estimated almost entirely from cross-window, cross-system differences under either batcher. Building the whole map with baseline_uniform instead of the slot27 batcher gives a numerically indistinguishable result: diff/shared 1.0106 vs 1.0117, foil/contentful-rand 0.2981 vs 0.3014. Batch composition also never concentrates: at full anneal (step 3000 of 4000) the batch still spans all 8 images, max 14 of 64 from one.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/rev27/p2.py (NN same-seq 0.010 vs 0.009, same-image 0.189 vs 0.135; weighted same-seq mass 0.008 vs 0.007), p3.py (image histogram per batch), p11.py (uniform-batcher rows).

divergences.claim: (hypothesis §3) 'Those two rules are DISJOINT by construction ... on this data they cover disjoint halves of it. In the cups windows ... the partner's rule structurally rejects every cups triple; only the parent's rule sees them ... only the partner's rule sees [cvar]' — and the crossover teaches the operator 'WHEN a command carries content unchanged (mv) and WHEN it rewrites it (redirect-append)'.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both coverage claims are false, and the failure is in the harmful direction. Running the head's own _mine_path_triples on real batches: 4898 triples over 8 batches, of which 1203 (24.6%) lie entirely inside cups steps. Their dominant verb signatures are ('cat','mv','mv') 678 and ('mv','mv','cat') 315 — the change rule is supervising the shared transition operator that an mv command maps a file's content INTO the constant empty-mv observation, and maps the constant empty-mv observation INTO a file's content. That is the exact opposite of 'mv carries content unchanged', on the pack the objective is scored on. Symmetrically, the preserving rule mines 775 cvar triples out of 1490, not zero. The rules are disjoint as triples (one requires a duplicate pair, the other requires change >= floor) but they do not partition the data as claimed.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/rev27/p9.py and p10.py, using the head's own _mine_path_triples with its own defaults (path_thresh 0.60, path_change_floor 0.25) on collated real batches: pack triple counts {(cvar,cvar,cvar):3655, (cups,cups,cups):1203, (other,other,other):40}; preserving-rule mined 1490 = {cvar:775, cups:512, other:203}.

divergences.claim: (hypothesis §2) 'The map multiplies squared error along a direction by g^2 = (mu/mean(mu))^p, so up to a bounded factor 9 between the most and the least discriminative direction.'
divergences.what_the_code_does: The clamp is on g, not g^2: gain.clamp(1/3, 3) bounds the squared-error ratio at 81, not 9. Measured actual ratio (1.8234/0.3404)^2 = 28.7.

divergences.claim: Numbers the author states from reading evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: 'About a third of all training targets in this sample are that one exactly-duplicated vector' and 'cvar steps are about 40% of all steps'.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both are honest and close. The rendered observation 'cwd=/ exit=0\n' is 227 of 724 steps = 31.4% of the sample, and 2618 of 7606 = 34.4% of encoded observations in the held-out split are one bit-identical vector. Steps whose command touches /tmp/w/cvar are 338 of 724 = 46.7%, stated as 'about 40%'.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad counts over evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl; scratchpad/rev27/p4.py 'modal dup count 2618 of 7606'.
